purpose: Concept previews for the first UI interview round; not runtime screenshots or acceptance evidence.

environment.fidelity: ImageGen approximates configured typography and terminal proportions; it does not guarantee pixel-accurate font rasterization or cell geometry.

outputs.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a highly faithful terminal UI concept image, not a poster. The attached image is a style reference from the user's actual Pi terminal. Use its Pi text rendering, modest font weight, native text colors, pale tool output blocks. Remove all fixture/demo text and startup theme listing. Create a fresh realistic work scenario.
Canvas: 1536x1024, landscape, edge-to-edge terminal content, no outer window chrome or rounded window frame. Approximate a 150-column x 50-row Ghostty terminal at 12pt. Flat solid background #eff1f5; foreground #4c4f69; accent teal #179299; blue #1e66f5; muted gray #8c8fa1; amber #df8e1d; thin rules #ccd0da; cursor #dc8a78. Font JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono, fallback Symbols Nerd Font Mono, then LXGW WenKai Mono. Monospaced, slightly thickened, no ligatures, compact ~18-20px line spacing, English only. Very small 6px left/right content inset; align all left edges. No gradients, shadow, browser cards, tabs, sidebar, overlay, demo labels, annotations or legend.
The main conversation is realistic English. From top to about y=430, show these blocks, with modest vertical gaps:
User message on light gray rectangle, 2 lines:
"Review subagent worktree recovery against the upstream package."
"Run two investigations in parallel, then have a reviewer compare the findings."
Assistant text, 2 lines:
"I'll trace recovery and inspect upstream behavior in parallel."
"The reviewer will start when both reports are ready."
Pale mint tool block, three lines:
"subagent"
"Started lifecycle and packages."
"reviewer is waiting for both reports."
Assistant text:
"While they work, I'll check the recovery decision we already agreed on."
Pale mint read-tool block, 4 lines:
"read docs/subagents-redevelopment.md"
"Continue from the subagent's previous workspace and branch."
"If only the worktree directory was removed, restore it from that branch."
"If the required code state cannot be recovered, report the failure."
Assistant text:
"I'll check whether recovery can silently fall back to the main directory."
All text must be legible and spelled correctly. The scene is illustrative task progress, not a completed run.
STATE 1: Main agent screen with compact FleetView at the very bottom.
After the conversation, leave natural empty terminal space. At around y=755 show main activity "Checking the recovery path..." in muted text.
At y=780 to y=835, show the native MAIN input editor: two thin full-width horizontal rules, a single draft line between them "Also check what happens when the branch is missing." An unobtrusive caret at end, not a big input panel.
Immediately below the editor are TWO statusline rows:
row 1 left "~/dev/pi-stuff (codex/subagent-implementation)"
row 2 left "↑24k ↓3.1k $0.031 9%/272k"
row 2 far right "(openai-codex) gpt-6-astra · medium"
Below the statusline, the full-width FleetView has FOUR rows. Use only selection circles, with lifecycle selected as a filled circle and all others hollow. No row background selection, no bold selected name, no left gutter. Main has no description or stats.
Exact row content, arranged as shared aligned terminal columns:
"○ main"
"● lifecycle     Trace worktree recovery" and far right "34s · ↓ 1.8k tokens"
"○ packages      Compare upstream behavior" and far right "31s · ↓ 1.4k tokens"
"○ reviewer      Review both findings" and state "Waiting" aligned just before the time column; no elapsed or tokens for this unstarted task.
Name starts and description starts align in all child rows. The circles begin at exactly the same left x as statusline text. The numeric time columns and down arrows and tokens text align across active rows, statistics end at the right content edge. No "Running", no task numbers.
A final muted footer line at bottom reads "j/k select · Enter inspect · Esc back". Keep all rows fully visible. The fleet occupies the entire bottom width and is BELOW statusline. No other fleet or UI duplicate.
